options.reason: Annual deaths show the absolute fatality burden directly recorded in the crash data.
options.answer: The data cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual number of motorists killed changed, and the chart shows a decrease from 110 deaths in 2013 to 81 in 2025. Annual death totals are a defensible measure of fatality burden, but they leave the per-mile risk question unanswered because miles driven are not in the data.

options.metric: Motorist deaths per 100,000 police-reported crash reports
options.denominator: All police-reported crash rows in the year, scaled to 100,000
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by crash-report volume gives a crash-based comparison that accounts for changes in the number of reported crashes.
options.answer: Per-mile risk is unmeasured; motorist deaths per 100,000 crash reports rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This framing compares motorist deaths with annual crash-report volume, and the chart shows an increase from 54.0 deaths per 100,000 reports in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025. It is a defensible crash-normalized measure because each row is a reported crash, but it leaves the per-mile risk question unanswered because the data contain no miles driven.

answer:
The crash data cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; annual motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 ([chart](out/option_1.png)).
Per-mile risk is unmeasured; motorist deaths per 100,000 crash reports rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025 ([chart](out/option_2.png)).
